data: Which of the following graphs is a heatmap?

The question asks which of the given graphs is a heatmap. A heatmap typically represents data using color gradients or shades to indicate values. In this case, the figure contains several subfigures, but none of them appear to be heatmaps. The subfigures (a), (b), and (c) show distributions of utterance lengths for different authors and movies, represented by lines and colors, but they do not use color gradients to represent data values. The subfigures (d), (e), and (f) show distributions of utterance lengths for different datasets, also represented by lines and colors, but again, they do not use color gradients to represent data values. Subfigure (g) shows a distribution of utterance lengths for a dataset, represented by a line and a shaded area, but it does not use color gradients to represent data values either. Therefore, none of the graphs in the figure are heatmaps.
